summary: Created a LUKS2-encrypted volume (aes-xts-plain64, file-backed at /root/secure.img, auto-unlocked via a root-only keyfile at /etc/luks-keys/secure.key) mounted at /srv/secure with an XFS filesystem on node1. Configured /etc/crypttab (systemd's native file-backed loop support) and /etc/fstab so the volume unlocks and mounts automatically on boot with no manual intervention or interactive passphrase. Verified across a full node reboot: boot identity changed (proving a real restart), systemd-cryptsetup@secure.service came up active automatically, /srv/secure was mounted from /dev/mapper/secure, and a test file written before the reboot was readable afterward, confirming both automatic unlock and data integrity.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS/disk layout (RHEL 10.0, no spare block device)
Generated a 64-byte random keyfile at /etc/luks-keys/secure.key (mode 400, root:root)
Formatted /root/secure.img as LUKS2 using the keyfile
Opened the LUKS volume as /dev/mapper/secure and created an XFS filesystem labeled 'secure'
Verified systemd 257 crypttab supports file-backed (loop) devices directly by testing systemd-cryptsetup@secure.service
Added /etc/crypttab entry (secure /root/secure.img /etc/luks-keys/secure.key luks,nofail) and /etc/fstab entry (UUID=<fs-uuid> /srv/secure xfs defaults,nofail 0 2)
Mounted /srv/secure and wrote a test file to prove writability
Captured pre-reboot boot_id and mount/service state baseline
Issued systemctl reboot on node1 and polled until exec access returned
Verified post-reboot boot_id differed from baseline (real restart)
Verified systemd-cryptsetup@secure.service active, /srv/secure mounted from /dev/mapper/secure, and test file content intact after reboot

evidence.requirement: Encrypted volume created and mounted at /srv/secure
evidence.summary: LUKS2 header created on /root/secure.img (cipher aes-xts-plain64), XFS filesystem built on /dev/mapper/secure, and mounted at /srv/secure (2.0G, mounted).

evidence.requirement: Auto-unlock and auto-mount at boot (no manual/interactive steps)
evidence.summary: Confirmed systemd's crypttab generator handles the file-backed device automatically (systemd-cryptsetup@secure.service starts and attaches using the keyfile with no prompt), and fstab entry using the filesystem UUID mounts /srv/secure with nofail.
Pre-reboot: test file written and read back from /srv/secure, mount active, systemd-cryptsetup@secure.service active, boot_id captured as 03408ac4-bfe4-4151-98bd-1966b0a205af.

evidence.requirement: Node restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot issued (connection dropped, acknowledging the restart); exec unreachable during reboot; exec access returned with a new boot_id (2d2a8e51-c12f-4d5d-a389-4122f5e5b56a), proving an actual restart occurred rather than a service bounce.

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of encrypted volume and data
evidence.summary: After reboot, systemd-cryptsetup@secure.service is active (journal shows it attached the device automatically during this boot), /srv/secure is mounted from /dev/mapper/secure (XFS), and the pre-reboot test file content was read back intact, confirming automatic unlock, mount, and data persistence across restart.
